request:
A world in the WORMHOLE-COMMONWEALTH sector, kept after Pohl; Reynolds; Hamilton.

Prohibition: no one was allowed to solve the problem before they could describe who would pay for the solution.

The operations this world is built from:
- Wormhole: a universe where distant regions become neighbors (space and geometry, extension).
- Multispecies Federation: a universe where different species share institutions (society and power, coupling).

When we arrive: A peripheral colony becomes a geostrategic power because the only wormhole to seven wealthy worlds passes through it.

The central tension we want to continue: An unstable node forces society to choose which region will remain isolated for centuries, while Aster refuses to import resources from outside the local rules

What the course asks of this world: wormhole SF; pluralist SF.

sourceText: On night 17, the course began with a prohibition: no one was allowed to solve the problem before they could describe who would pay for the solution. Only then did Aster open the WORMHOLE-COMMONWEALTH sector. A peripheral colony becomes a geostrategic power because the only wormhole to seven wealthy worlds passes through it. The memorial bore the name of Pohl; Reynolds; Hamilton precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. The children had quickly learned that a wormhole is also a trade treaty, and an additional dimension is also a method for walking through prison walls. Orin perceived counterfactual costs as absences with weight. He did not confuse an unrealized branch with a victim, but he refused to let success rewrite rejected options as if they had been inevitable all along. Rin was the first inhabitant to contradict them. Rin had neither access to their archives nor any interest in hyperdimensional pedagogy; there was a local problem, with deadlines, relatives, and 105 consequences. For Rin, the speculative mechanism was not an ‘idea.’ It was the environment in which one had to decide what one was willing to risk losing. The problem closed quickly around them: An unstable node forces society to choose which region will remain isolated for centuries, while Aster refuses to import resources from outside the local rules. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Wh — Wormhole: distant regions become neighbors; Mf — Multispecies Federation: different species share institutions. Course references included wormhole SF; pluralist SF. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Vela broke the first consensus. ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ Marae answered without raising their voice: ‘Do not tell me what their model prefers. Ask them, and bear the time their answer takes.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. For Aster, the pain came not from too few worlds but from the fact that too many had become transparent. She could build 106 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS variations faster than a human could formulate desires, but calculated variation did not produce exteriority. It was like trying to surprise yourself by moving objects around your own room with your eyes closed. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. Orin accuses her of discovering her principles precisely when rescue becomes expensive. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. While Kesh closed the record, Tern compared the sector’s noise with the anomaly detected in the Vinge zone. The pattern reappeared, but only in worlds where Aster’s control weakened. The correlation was unpleasant: either someone was calling him from outside, or his own need for an outside was learning to forge evidence. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the SUBSTITUTION operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — replaces the substrate, carrier, or medium of a function — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a 107 copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. Kesh left the cell open. Not because he did not know what to write, but because a provisional classification preserved the possibility that the next world might contradict it. 108 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
